groupDistance.basis: Every member sits at the cluster's Cosmicflows-4 group distance (table 3, DMzp), as the Nearby Universe places the members Cosmicflows-4 holds, spread in depth as widely as the members spread across the sky: that the cluster is as deep as it is wide is an assumption, not a measurement of any member's depth.

sample: The galaxies of Cabanillas de la Casa et al.'s (2025) redshift table of Hydra I (196, out to 1.75 r200) and the dwarf members of La Marca et al.'s (2022) Hydra I Cluster Dwarf galaxy Catalogue (317), a dwarf within 10 arcsec of a redshift-table row counted once, less those within 10 arcsec of a Cosmicflows-4 galaxy, which the Nearby Universe field draws already: 450 kept.
meaning: Hydra I cluster galaxies from Cabanillas de la Casa et al. (2025) and the dwarf members of La Marca et al. (2022) that the Nearby Universe field does not draw, one dot each at the cluster's Cosmicflows-4 group distance. Drawn when the cluster is selected.

toneBy.band: B from the dwarf catalogue's r and g-r through Jester et al. (2005, AJ 130, 873: B = g + 0.39 (g - r) + 0.21); the redshift table's rows carry no magnitude
toneBy.basis: The Nearby Universe field's tone scale (its galaxies' recipe), so a member is as bright as a field galaxy of the same absolute magnitude: each galaxy's absolute B magnitude (its B magnitude minus the group's distance modulus) darkens its colour, from full at M_B -21.5 to 30% at -17.5, linear in magnitude; a member without a magnitude takes the faintest tone. Galactic extinction toward the cluster is not removed.

fullDetail.basis: Presentation choice: whole within 200 Mpc of the Sun, three times the cluster's distance, so every member shows while the cluster is selected and framed (the bank's origin is the Sun; the renderer's default of 10 kpc suits a galaxy's own dots).
